note: The path grammar: M L Q C Z O. It is shared by the bots' looks, the animation format, nlook shapes and the keyboard's `path` mark, so one set of cases keeps four parsers honest: NLookPath.swift, NLookPaint.kt, KBPath.swift and KbPath.kt. The Swift and Kotlin parser cores are kept byte-identical inside marked regions, and CI diffs them.

cases.why: Move, two lines, close. The oldest shape there is.
The quadratic the bots' looks format 1 already uses everywhere.

C is the animation spec's format-2 addition (C c1x c1y c2x c2y x y). Every native parser accepts it FROM DAY ONE, so a path drawn for an animation scene stays drawable as a widget shape or a key print without waiting for a second build.
O is a circle: cx cy r. The bots' looks use it for dots and puffs.
Repeated commands without repeating the letter, as the looks file already writes them.
An unknown command drops ONLY that path, never the shape around it and never the design. Arcs are not in the grammar: C covers what we need and keeps every parser small.
A command with the wrong count of numbers is not guessed at.
A token that is not a number drops the path. There is no expression evaluation anywhere in this format.
A path is 900 characters at most, and a Shape holds at most 12 of them. On Android each path becomes an alpha-mask bitmap, so a path is not free.
Over twelve, the extras are dropped and the shape still draws.
The same path as a key print: `path` is the one new mark shape in this build, beside the rect, line, circle and bars that already ship.
